To: docs/climate-programme/border-revenues-launch/handover
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT — Thursday launch handover for Inês — not yet shared

Inês,

I am taking the train to the Netherlands tonight. My father is ill, I am with my family. I don’t yet know how long I’ll be away, so please plan to lead Thursday’s launch without me.

I’m sorry. Finding the figure 3 error this afternoon and then leaving you with the corrections, the press and the event is a horrible handover. The 2.1 mistake is mine, not yours. Please say that if anyone asks; you do not need to take responsibility for it on my behalf.

I trust you completely with this. You know the paper as well as I do, and you ran the annex B sensitivity runs yourself. You do not need to wait for me to approve every decision. What follows is the order I would tackle things in, with the things that must not get lost.

1. First priority: correct the number everywhere, especially with the press

The correct 2030 estimate for LDC-relevant revenue is EUR 1.4 billion, not EUR 2.1 billion. Figure 3 and the summary had picked up the old run, which did not apply the free-allocation phase-out. The paper’s conclusion does not change, but its headline number does. We should be straightforward about both parts, not make the correction sound smaller than it is.

The PDF v7 in the launch folder is already corrected on pages 3, 14 and 15. Use that as the reference version.

Still outstanding:
- Deck v4: correct slides 6 and 9, including the revenue chart on slide 9. Check the speaker notes too, since my old notes are still in the deck.
- The embargoed press release: Hanna sent the version with EUR 2.1 billion to 34 Brussels contacts on Friday. Those journalists need an explicit correction, not just a silently replaced attachment.
- Check any launch summary or other material we intend to publish against PDF v7 so we don’t put the old number back into circulation.

Please contact Hanna first, as soon as you can. Ask her to arrange a corrected release and send a clear correction to everyone who received Friday’s version, with the corrected paper. The embargo lifts Thursday 26 November at 10:00 CET, so this needs to happen before then, preferably well before journalists finish their stories.

Suggested factual wording, if useful:

“We have corrected the 2030 estimate for LDC-relevant CBAM revenue from EUR 2.1 billion to EUR 1.4 billion. The earlier figure came from an older model run that did not apply the free-allocation phase-out. The corrected paper is PDF v7; the paper’s conclusion is unchanged.”

If someone asks whose error it was: “This was Marieke’s error, not Inês’s.” That is the truth.

Geert knows I am away. If Hanna needs a senior name to sign off the corrected release, he can do that. Please don’t let waiting for me hold up the correction.

2. Next: agree the revised event arrangements with Tomás

The run of show in the folder is no longer quite right. Tomás emailed this morning: Katarina Lindqvist now has to leave at 13:30 because of a vote. He has asked for a 15-minute presentation, rather than 20, and the panel to begin at 12:50. She wants to take at least two questions herself before leaving.

Please confirm that you will present and take my panel place, and agree the revised running order with him. In particular, clarify when those questions will happen and who will moderate after 13:30 if the event continues to 14:00. The old schedule puts Q&A at 13:40, which won’t meet her request.

The fixed points we currently have are:
- Thursday 26 November, European Parliament, Altiero Spinelli building; room booked by Lindqvist’s office.
- Guests at the security entrance by 12:00; Tomás collects badges.
- Light lunch outside the room from 12:00.
- 12:30: Lindqvist’s welcome, five minutes.
- 12:35: your presentation, now 15 minutes.
- 12:50: panel starts.
- Lindqvist leaves at 13:30, having taken at least two questions.
- Original close: 14:00, subject to confirming the revised arrangements.

The security deadline is Wednesday 25 November at 12:00. Tomás needs the final names of everyone attending from our side by then; otherwise they will not get in. Please make sure the list reflects the change from me to you and includes anyone helping on the day. Don’t assume an email about the speaker change also updates the badge list.

3. Wednesday: press calls and a short, corrected presentation

Hanna promised two journalists calls with me on Wednesday afternoon: one from a trade newsletter and one from a Belgian daily. My calendar has 14:00 and 15:00, 20 minutes each, but both are marked “Hanna to confirm”.

Please ask Hanna to confirm the journalists and timings, explain that I am unavailable, and arrange for you to take the calls if you can. If they clash with essential preparation, agree another arrangement with her rather than trying to squeeze everything in. Make sure both journalists have the correction before the call and know which PDF to use.

For the presentation, cut to 15 minutes rather than trying to deliver the existing 20-minute talk faster. Lead with the question the paper answers and the main finding, give the corrected revenue estimate, and leave enough room for the policy implications. You know what matters here. There is no obligation to preserve my speaker notes or my way of saying it.

4. Panel preparation: be open on the assumptions, but keep the frame

Kessler has already said he will challenge the 80% downstream steel-user pass-through assumption and resource shuffling. Be ready for it, but don’t let him turn the whole launch into a debate about one central-case assumption.

The lines in my note still stand:
- 80% is the central case, not a claim that every firm can pass through that much.
- Annex B tests 60% and 40%.
- The result holds at 60% and weakens at 40%. Say that plainly; don’t imply it is equally strong across all cases.
- On resource shuffling, we agree it is a risk. Section 5.2 addresses it, and we recommend the Commission’s monitoring report.

Answer his point, acknowledge the limitation, then bring the discussion back to the paper’s findings and the implications for LDCs. You ran those sensitivities yourself; you don’t need to defend them as someone else’s work.

Abena Owusu-Mensah is joining remotely from the Accra Trade Policy Centre. The link is in the calendar invite and was tested successfully, according to your deck notes. Please check she knows about the earlier panel start and that whoever is handling the room can connect her. She was strong on the LDC side in our call, but don’t assume she will answer for us or necessarily agree with every point.

And please remember Lisbon. At the COP side event, when the projector died, you rescued my panel. You are better live than you think. Thursday does not require you to impersonate me.

5. On the day, and the small follow-up that is easy to miss

Before Thursday’s 10:00 CET embargo lift, check with Hanna that the correction has gone to the original press list and that the release and any publication materials use EUR 1.4 billion and PDF v7. Take the corrected deck, not an older local copy.

Allow time for Parliament security and a room/remote-link check. Keep the revised running order somewhere you can see it, especially the questions before Lindqvist leaves.

Lucy Tran from Halvorsen is attending with a colleague. For the grant report she needs two event photos and attendance numbers, ideally by 4 December. Please arrange in advance who will take the photos and record attendance so this doesn’t become another job you have to remember while speaking.

Availability and what to say about my absence

You can call me. After 09:00 tomorrow, Tuesday, I might not pick up, and I can’t promise quick replies after that. Please leave a message if something needs my attention, but use Geert for the corrected-release sign-off and make the launch decisions you need to make without waiting for me.

If anyone asks why I am away, please keep it to: “My father is ill, I am with my family.” Nothing further about him.

I am sorry to leave you with this much at such short notice. I know trusting you doesn’t make the extra work disappear. But I do trust you, completely: with the paper, with the room, and with deciding what needs to give if there isn’t time for everything.

Marieke
